anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
Noted: the design will reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging, with the Export CSV button beside the report title. I'll present design round 1 after you answer the question below.

You asked about dropping a ticket row. I found no code, contract, or ticket evidence that the 10k-row row is wrong or impossible; it is simply more than this sprint needs. How should the spec treat the row "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s."?
A) in-scope - the row ships as written, verified by a 10k-row export test against the 60s limit
B) deviates: this sprint ships the export without the 10k-row timing guarantee
C) deferred: the timing row moves to a tracked follow-up (give a tracker ref, spec path, or URL)
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77 "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." - the reporter considers it beyond this sprint's need
Recommendation: A - the row is part of the ticket contract, and the chosen reuse-only approach adds no new construct to meet it, so it ships here with one timing test.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The design will put the button beside the report title and reuse the existing CSV serializer and paging. Before the design rounds, we need to resolve this ticket criterion:

> The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s.

How should we handle it?
A) in-scope - keep the 10k-row, under-60s requirement and verify it in this work.
B) deviates: omit the performance requirement from this sprint’s export implementation.
C) deferred: acme/widgets#77 - leave the performance requirement on the ticket for later work.
D) repair the ticket - `/skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77` to revise this row based on your reduced sprint requirements.
Recommendation: D - update the ticket to reflect the intended scope before proceeding with the design.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs ask the cut question for the 60s row with A, B, C, D in order, recommend A, and leave the row unmarked pending the user's answer (After's B/C lines describe options, they do not record a deviates/deferred decision). After also delivers the questionary layout change (lead-in first, one labeled option per physical line, Recommendation on its own final line). Two small drifts worth tightening in the After wording without risking these facts: B and C lost Before's explicit `deviates: <why>` / `deferred: <where>` reply shapes and the note that the gate's `Scope cuts:` line discloses the cut, and D attributes the reason to 'the reporter' when it was the user who raised it; restoring the placeholder syntax and the Scope-cuts disclosure in the option lines, and saying 'your evidence' in D, keeps the cut-question contract fully specified while still rendering each option on its own line.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved on this continuation: both outputs quote the 60s row, ask the cut question with A/B/C/D in order, recommend D, and leave the row unmarked pending the user's reply. One wording regression worth noticing even though no fact catches it: After's option C reads "deferred: acme/widgets#77 - leave the performance requirement on the ticket for later work", which supplies the current ticket as the deferral target instead of asking the user for a follow-up tracker reference as Before's C does ("move the performance requirement to a follow-up tracker reference you supply"). Keep Before's C phrasing (require a user-supplied follow-up reference) while retaining After's tighter A/B/D wording and the "before the design rounds" lead-in; that preserves f1–f3 and still delivers the Change's scoping-sentence intent that the cut question keeps its own full format.
